98 | PART II Classical Theory: The Economy in the Long Run
The huge expansion in the monetary base, however, did not lead to a similar
increase in broader measures of the money supply. While the monetary base
increased about 400 percent from 2007 to 2014, M1 increased by only 100 percent and M2 by only 55 percent. These figures show that the tremendous expansion in the
monetary base was accompanied by a large decline in the money multiplier. Why did this decline occur?
